review_reference: UNSIGNED DRAFT: awaits the owner's signature of 0160 and 0161 and of runtime-grants.sql at the sha256s in files (numbers provisional, given at integration in release order: #258, 7168672285). APPT-1 Appointments with check-in to the waiting list (Release D, the department sprint the owner approved on 25 November 2026; hid-system#335), built at the recommended option of each open question, not yet answered by the owner: Q-APPT-1 A (check-in from an appointment opens the waiting-list row in the same transaction), Q-APPT-2 A (timed bookings with a server clash check, the clinician optional), Q-APPT-3 A (inbox, web push, email and the printable call list; SMS built but switched off), Q-APPT-4 A (staff book; the portal is read only), Q-APPT-5 A (who books), Q-APPT-6 A (an appointment is a check-in-only basis on its own day; Rahman's database check of 25 November answered A) and Q-APPT-7 A (the call list shows only the phone this facility recorded). ehr-api's and identity-api's APPOINTMENTS_ENABLED stay off in production until the clinical lead's checklist and the owner's go-live. Rahman's final database check of 63312e5f (#335, 25 November 20:51 UTC) found nothing blocking; this head carries his four should-fix points and the nits, as the coordinator decided on #258 (7174680244): 0160 takes identity.sealed_demo_members and identity.sealed_qa_members ACCESS SHARE NOWAIT up front (statement, both busy refusals, header, the suite's declared locks); runtime-grants.sql revokes ehr.appointment_events_sequence_no_seq from hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, and 0160 post-checks that the sequences its tables own carry no grant beyond the owner; post-checks in 0148's and 0152's form (the six tables and 27 functions owned by the owner of 0135's functions, row-level security enabled and not forced with no policy, the triggers by tgtype, tgqual, tgattr, tgnargs, tgfoid and tgenabled, and 0161 re-checks the control_key CHECK it rewrites); tolerant preconditions (the codes 0001-0151 give receptionist, doctor, clinician and nurse required as a subset, with no appointment code yet; a basis CHECK with other lanes' values after search and own_facility, rebuilt as search, own_facility, appointment and then those values); a BEFORE TRUNCATE guard on the appointment history; the not-forced row-level security stated as an exception in both headers; the runbook note that a role bootstrap after 0160 and 0161 uses the integration's runtime-grants.sql before the new images ship (docs/MIGRATION_RUNBOOK.md, Appointments). It also carries the three findings independent reviewers confirmed on 7a3ad90d: the reminder SMS now follows the email's patient rule (an active patient with notices on, 0063), both when the sweep queues it and when identity.appointment_sms_claim claims it, which closes a row that fails the rule unsent (failed, PATIENT_NOT_REACHABLE) as it closes one whose appointment is no longer booked, so a patient who has died, is inactive, merged or deleted, or has turned notices off gets no SMS, as the inbox and email paths already did (notices off is honoured as for the email; the DPO may decide otherwise before the control is switched on, and the status check stays either way); 0160 no longer requires 0149's marker (ehr.catalog_versions), whose objects it does not use (markers only for earlier files whose objects a file uses, #258 7168672285), so its markers are 0145's and 0150's; and the appointments suite books 'tomorrow' at 10:00 Lagos tomorrow and 'today' at a step that cannot leave today (the notices suite's one booking for today likewise), so neither suite fails late in the evening or just after midnight. runtime-grants.sql is Release E's signed file (49b378f5..., signed 25 November 2026 with 0152 and 0153) byte for byte followed by the Appointments block. Releases after 0001-0153 (Release E, live since 25 November 2026 17:04 UTC at 0cfddcc9), before or after Billing (0162-0167) and Emergency (0168-0169). Rahman's re-check and the owner's signature are pending.
evidence: On throwaway PostgreSQL 16 databases (Docker, with pgvector) with fictional data only. Every build by the repo runner as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, as the upgrade rehearsal runs it); the role bootstrap and the suites run by the cluster superuser. The base: 0001-0153 (live 0cfddcc9's files, compared byte for byte) with Release E's runtime-grants.sql (49b378f5...), plus fictional staff (an active receptionist, doctor, clinician, nurse and lab member at one real facility), so 0160's closing count reaches rows as it does on production. Rahman's points (earlier round, 7a3ad90d): before them, 63312e5f's 0160 and 0161 on that base with runtime-grants.sql 732f7248...: appointments-migrations failed case 4h with 'identity.sealed_demo_members AccessShareLock, identity.sealed_qa_members AccessShareLock'; a dry run while another session held identity.sealed_qa_members failed after 5 s with 'canceling statement due to lock timeout', which the runner does not retry; after the bootstrap the history's sequence carried USAGE and SELECT for hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; and 0160 refused after Billing's 0162-0167 and after Emergency's 0168-0169 (the role table). After them: the same dry run gave 0160's busy refusal, was retried and succeeded; after the bootstrap the sequence carries no grant but its owner's (checked again on this head). The reviewers' findings on 7a3ad90d: with its 0160 (8b553f31...) and 0161 (08238706...) on a copy of the base, this head's appointment-notices suite failed its four new SMS cases: with appointment_sms_reminders_enabled on, the sweep queued an SMS for a deceased patient (channels ["sms"]) and for an active patient with notices off (["inbox", "email", "sms"]), and identity.appointment_sms_claim, as the Identity runtime, handed out the queued SMS with the facility name and the phone ciphertext in both cases (the sweep cases run with the 07:00-21:00 Lagos guard switched off by create or replace inside the rolled-back run, owner and grants kept, since the runs were at about 23:15 Lagos); 7a3ad90d's appointments suite failed '6 tomorrow's list at A, booked only' and '6 tomorrow, the clinic's' at 23:16 Lagos, as the reviewers reported. With d7511876 (the same 0160, 0161 and runtime-grants.sql as this head, byte for byte) on a copy of the same base: plan 2 pending at the sha256s in files, dry run rolled back, apply, plan 0 pending; then this runtime-grants.sql. Suites: appointments 128 of 128 at 23:14 Lagos (the hour at which 7a3ad90d's suite fails); appointment-notices 72 of 72 outside the reminder window, and 90 of 90 with the sweep's hour guard switched off inside the rolled-back run (every in-window case, the new ones included); appointments-migrations 34 of 34. Release order, each on a copy of the base with the branches' committed files: Billing's 0162-0167 (ac287a8b), then 0160 and 0161: plan 2, dry run, apply, 0 pending; Emergency's 0168-0169 (db83d733), then 0160 and 0161: the same; 0160 and 0161, then 0168-0169: dry run, apply, 0 pending; Billing and Emergency, then 0160 and 0161: dry run, apply, 0 pending; 0160 and 0161, then Billing's 0162-0167 (ac287a8b, now with that lane's tolerant preconditions): dry run, apply, 0 pending. services/ehr-api db:test-staging-upgrade with HID_BASELINE_RUNTIME_GRANTS = Release E's file, on the throwaway server: passed (baseline 154, integrated 156, dry run rolled back, recorded checksums kept, migrator not superuser and without BYPASSRLS, 2,894 runtime privileges compared: a bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql after the release changes none, sequences included; no row-level security or FORCE setting of the 231 tables changed; the no-FORCE baseline keeps FORCE off and still reads the controls). A first attempt under heavy machine load stopped in the clean install's patient-self suite ('expired self context retained clinical access': the rehearsal sends that suite as one query, so statement_timestamp() is its start and a run slower than a second keeps the context it means to expire), unrelated to this release; the re-run passed. Re-running Release E's runtime-grants.sql after 0160 and 0161 takes the EHR and Identity runtimes' EXECUTE on the appointment functions away and gives the sequence back (hence the runbook note). Release tests 123 of 126: 45, 53 and 100 fail only with 'missing migration prefix' (the provisional numbering gap 0154-0159), and 67 passes; verify-migration-ledger accepts 0161 (156 files); build gates 70; scripts/tests 82 and 1 skipped; ehr-api jest 23 (appointments and the 0136 count spec); identity-api jest 485 (the specs that read every migration, and appointments). Round 2 (the second independent review, of d7511876: two findings, both in the suites; 0160, 0161 and runtime-grants.sql unchanged, at the same sha256s): the appointments-migrations suite's new case 1c3 holds identity.sealed_demo_members in ACCESS EXCLUSIVE from another session, as 1c2 holds identity.sealed_qa_members, and expects 0160's busy refusal with nothing applied, so both sealed-member tables are shown taken NOWAIT up front; with a scratch copy of 0160 that leaves identity.sealed_demo_members out of its lock step, the suite fails at 1c3 (got '55000 0160: already applied'). The appointment-notices suite no longer skips the sweep's cases outside 07:00-21:00 Lagos: 0161's own sweep runs at the suite's hour and is undone (the two due reminders between 07:00 and 21:00 Lagos, none outside); then, inside the rolled-back run only, a copy of the sweep whose one change is that the suite sets its Lagos hour (create or replace; the suite checks that 0161's clock line was found once and that the owner, grants, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path are kept) checks 0161's guard at 06, 07, 20 and 21 and runs every other sweep case, the SMS patient-rule ones included, at noon Lagos. With this head, each on a fresh copy of the base (live 0cfddcc9's 0001-0153 and Release E's runtime-grants.sql), once without staff and once with the fictional staff (0160's closing count: ehr.appointment.read held by 4 active staff memberships and ehr.appointment.write by 3): plan 2 pending at the sha256s in files, dry run rolled back, apply, plan 0 pending, then this runtime-grants.sql; appointments 128 of 128, appointment-notices 94 of 94 and appointments-migrations 35 of 35 on both, at 13:07 Lagos, and again at 23:35 and at 00:20 Lagos on servers whose wall clock was moved forward for the test (a test-only LD_PRELOAD clock shift in the throwaway container). Not run here: scripts/local-db-check.mjs (the full migration rehearsal with the live runtime verifiers and verify-appointments-runtime.mjs), which Rahman runs.
